venues.name: Instagram (Reels, Stories, Broadcast channel)
venues.notes: Owned account, so self-promotion is the format; the constraint is reach, not rules. Captions hold 2,200 chars but only the first ~125 show before 'more', and NOTHING in a caption is clickable, so the CTA is 'link in bio' and the URL (1234tools.com/<section>/<slug>) must be burned into the video as a text overlay or a QR in the last second. Stories allow a link sticker (any account) and Broadcast channels allow links; use Stories for the day's tool. Reels of 7-15 s showing a before/after (blurry 8 MB photo -> 300 KB, PDF merged in two taps, 'stop paying for a PDF subscription') outperform talking heads. 3-5 hashtags in the caption, not a block of 30; alt-text and on-screen captions count for discovery. Reels are reposted to Facebook automatically if the accounts are linked. Repeated identical captions and link-spam in comments get reach throttled, not banned. Use a Linktree-style /go/ page on the site itself so bio links carry UTM parameters.
venues.verifiedHow: from memory — Instagram help pages are not machine-readable; verify caption and link-sticker behaviour before first post
venues.estimatedReach: unknown — depends on the owned account; Reels are shown to non-followers
venues.tone: show-don't-tell, one tool per Reel, plain words, no hype

venues.name: TikTok
venues.notes: Captions now allow 4,000 chars but the algorithm reads the first line and the spoken/on-screen text; keep captions short with 3-5 hashtags (#freetools #studytok #smallbusinesstips). Links in captions are not clickable; a clickable bio link needs a Business account or 1,000 followers, so the site URL must be on screen (text overlay for the whole clip) and the hook must be the result ('this free site removes a background in 2 seconds, no sign-up'). Screen-recorded phone how-tos of 7-15 s, 'stop paying for X' and 'you don't need an app for this' are the shapes that get pushed. Posting daily for the first month matters more than production quality. Reposting the same clip across TikTok, Reels and Shorts is normal; strip the TikTok watermark first (Shorts downranks it). Comment replies with links are hidden; reply with the site name only.

venues.estimatedReach: unknown — owned account; new accounts get a cold-start push on the For You feed
venues.tone: fast, casual, result first, no corporate voice

venues.notes: Owned channel: links ARE clickable in the description and in a pinned comment, so every video gets the tool URL with UTM in the first two description lines plus a pinned comment. Title max 100 chars; description 5,000; the first three #hashtags in the description show above the title. Shorts (under 3 min, vertical) feed discovery; 2-5 minute long-form 'how to merge PDFs free without uploading' videos rank in Google search for years and are the durable asset for a tools site. Chapters, a spoken 'no upload, runs in your browser' line, and an end screen pointing to the section hub work. Do not reupload TikTok-watermarked clips (downranked). Community posts (available once the channel is open) can carry links too. Channel description and 'links' box: use the /for/ collection pages.

Only comment where the uploader did not already promote a competing paid tool aggressively; never comment on tiny channels' videos with promotional text. Expect modest direct traffic; the value is branded search and the occasional creator who tries the tool and features it.

insights: Reach on every closed feed (X, LinkedIn, Facebook, TikTok, Instagram) is best when the post itself contains no external link: show the result as a screenshot or a 7-15 second screen recording, say the site name in the text and on screen, and put the UTM link in the first reply/comment, the bio, or the description. Bluesky, Mastodon, Threads, Pinterest, WhatsApp and Telegram do not penalise links — link inline there.

Content shapes that work for free browser tools, in order: (1) before/after with the numbers visible (8.2 MB -> 310 KB, 'no upload'); (2) 'stop paying for X' framed as your own story, never naming a competitor; (3) 7-second phone how-tos; (4) a result screenshot answering a real question someone just asked (reply-first); (5) checklists by job (month-end, start of term, year-end) linking a /for/ collection rather than a single tool.
One tool per post. A list of 1,281 tools is a blur; 'this one does GST on a bill in your browser, nothing uploaded, no account' is a share.

Truthful phrasing to use everywhere: 'runs in your browser', 'nothing you type is uploaded', 'no account', 'works offline once opened'. Never write 'no tracking' or 'no third-party requests' — analytics (GA4 + Clarity) load after the consent bar; on Mastodon and Bluesky an inexact privacy claim gets corrected publicly.

Cadence the platforms reward for a solo operator: TikTok/Reels/Shorts daily or near-daily for the first 30 days then 3-5/week (the same vertical clip goes to all three, de-watermarked); X and Threads daily short posts plus replies; LinkedIn 2-3 posts a week plus daily comments; Pinterest 5-10 pins a week forever; owned WhatsApp/Telegram channels 2-3 updates a week; each Discord server or Facebook/LinkedIn group at most one self-mention a fortnight and only after answering questions there.

What gets banned: identical text pasted into several groups/threads the same day; links in YouTube/TikTok/Instagram comments; posting in Facebook groups outside the promo thread; mentioning your site in a Discord help channel when it does not answer the question; buying followers or boosting an empty page. What gets throttled: link-only posts, hashtag walls (>5), TikTok-watermarked uploads on Shorts/Reels, posting more than once a day on LinkedIn.

Share-intent templates that accept prefilled text and are confirmed live today: WhatsApp https://wa.me/?text={text}; Telegram https://t.me/share/url?url={url}&text={text}; Threads https://www.threads.com/intent/post?text={text}; Mastodon https://mastodon.social/share?text={text}&url={url}; Pinterest https://www.pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url={url}&media={media}&description={text}; X https://x.com/intent/post?text={text}&url={url} (twitter.com/intent/tweet redirects); Bluesky https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text={text} (documented, SPA). URL-only: LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url={url} and Facebook https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u={url} (the quote= parameter is ignored). Also Reddit https://www.reddit.com/submit?url={url}&title={title}, Hacker News https://news.ycombinator.com/submitlink?u={url}&t={title}, email mailto:?subject={title}&body={text}%20{url}. Instagram, TikTok and YouTube have no web composer intent — the on-site share button should offer 'copy link' and navigator.share() for them.

For the on-site share button (the owner's actual request): per tool page emit og:title/og:description from build/jobs.js's verb + '≤110-char description', an og:image per section (or per tool when a result screenshot exists), and build the share text as '<tool title> — <description>. Free, runs in your browser: <url>?utm_source=share&utm_medium=<channel>&utm_campaign=<section>&utm_content=<slug>'. When a calculator has a result, prepend the result line ('GST on ₹1,00,000 at 18% = ₹18,000') so the shared message is useful on its own — WhatsApp and Telegram forwards of a result line are the highest-converting share on Indian and UK small-business audiences. Use navigator.share() when present (mobile), fall back to the intent URLs above, and always offer Copy link.

Timing across the three audiences in UTC: UK commute 06:30-08:30, UK lunch 12:00-13:30, India morning 03:30-05:30, India evening 13:30-16:30, US morning 13:00-15:00. The 13:00-15:00 UTC window hits UK afternoon, India evening and US morning at once and is the single best slot for LinkedIn, X and Threads.

Use UTM consistently: utm_source=<venue id above>, utm_medium=social|community|video|newsletter, utm_campaign=<section slug>, utm_content=<tool slug>. Shorten through an owned /go/ redirect on the site so bio links and spoken URLs stay memorable while still carrying attribution.

Pinterest and long-form YouTube are the compounding venues: a pin or a 3-minute how-to indexed by Google for 'free payslip generator uk' or 'cm to inches' keeps sending traffic for years, which matters more than any single viral Reel for a 1,281-tool directory. Budget a third of the weekly 3-5 hours there.

Discord and Facebook/LinkedIn groups are for listening and for one honest showcase post each; measure them by feature requests and bug reports (feed them into the tool-request form), not by clicks. Read a server's or group's rules channel in full before writing anything, and record what you read in this register's notes.
